_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated; see CLAUDE.md.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A beam between two cells, named in the record's own fields rather than drawn between blocks that happen to line up. It runs on one axis on all 117 in the game, and no block ever stands between its ends. One field gives that axis, another is read as whether it starts lit, and the type carries the colour, which is what pairs a laser with the button and teleporter of the same colour. Its ends carry the emitter blocks, and 61 of the 234 sit on cells the lattice leaves empty, which is the game placing geometry a level's own grid does not.

666.name: Start
666.note: Every level ends with exactly one of these, and it is the last record in the table. It carries the start cell, a second cell it looks at, two angles, and a number that is 99 on 218 of the 230 levels and lower on the other twelve, which reads as the level's time. It is not a thing standing on a block, so it draws as the start ring rather than as an object marker.

0/0.name: Blue coin
0/0.note: 1206 placed across 159 levels, the game's most numerous object. Absent from LEVEL 1, where no blue coin appears; it starts turning up from LEVEL 3.

0/30.name: Fruit
0/30.note: Exactly one in each of 173 levels and never two, which is the shape of the fruit slot. Which fruit stands in it is not in the level: no field here takes five values, and the game carries an uncollected fruit forward to the next level, so the choice is progress rather than data.

0/31.name: Key
0/31.note: One to four a level and never more: 66 levels with one, 40 with two, 7 with three, 1 with four. Collecting every key is what turns the exit from red to green.

0/37.name: Bronze coin
0/37.note: 1005 placed across 154 levels, up to 45 in one. LEVEL 1 holds exactly two, and the game shows exactly two bronze coins there.

8/0.name: Red laser
8/0.note: Seen in OBJ LEVEL: the vertical beam from the floating block to the floor, red at both ends and off until something turns it on. Every one of the nine in the game starts dark.

8/1.name: Green laser
8/1.note: Seen in OBJ LEVEL: the beam between the two floating blocks, green at both ends and lit. Colour is read as the type's rather than the start-state flag's; LEVEL 109 has four of these that start dark and settles which.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#18.note: 160 of its 178 blocks are not part of the level at all. They lie flat on z=32, the floor of the lattice and 22 blocks below the playable structure, spelling VERY WELL DONE in block letters six blocks tall.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developer object catalogue, shipped unchanged in nine of the ten worlds and never reached in play. One of nearly every object in the game stands on a flat floor: walk it in an emulator and each one names itself. `tools/kula_objlevel.py` writes the floor plan, and `tools/kula_warp.py` writes a disc copy that reaches it.
